answer: One concrete defense is a refundable identity bond. Each agent must lock a fixed stake, say 100 tokens, to a single on-chain identity before it can trade or vote; misbehavior is slashed. Spinning up 1,000 sybils then means posting 1,000 separate bonds, 100,000 tokens frozen, not one. In a market pricing timber, saffron, and pigment futures, honest agents post once and reclaim their bond, while an attacker's fleet bleeds value on every slash, so the sybil army costs far more than it can ever skim.
